metadata.file_name: TIMSS 2015 Grade 9 National Report South Africa.pdf
metadata.title: Understanding mathematics and science achievement amongst Grade 9 learners in South Africa
metadata.venue: HSRC Press (Human Sciences Research Council) / TIMSS South Africa website

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2015 Grade 9 South Africa microdata collected via a two-stage stratified cluster design (schools sampled with PPS, then intact Grade 9 classes within schools). The report describes the TIMSS achievement scaling procedure using five plausible values for mathematics and science, and it also reports multilevel (HLM) analyses for mathematics achievement. However, the manuscript text provided does not specify the application of student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the inferential models. Given the absence of explicit weight-variable names and the fact that the analysis is presented as national estimates and multilevel regression results, the weighting strategy cannot be verified from the provided text; therefore, weight usage is treated as not reported rather than assumed.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report states that TIMSS uses five plausible values for mathematics and science achievement, but it does not describe how missing data in questionnaire/context variables were handled (e.g., complete-case deletion vs imputation). This is a reporting gap because missingness handling can affect multilevel regression estimates and the interpretation of associations between learner/school factors and achievement.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the TIMSS 2015 Grade 9 South Africa national sample drawn from the 2013 DBE master list of schools offering Grade 9. Sampling followed TIMSS two-stage stratified cluster procedures: 300 schools were sampled (292 participated) and, within each participating school, an intact Grade 9 class was selected (two classes in dual-medium schools). The analytic sample for the report’s multilevel mathematics effectiveness analysis is the set of 12,514 Grade 9 learners from 292 schools who participated in the main administration; no additional exclusion criteria (e.g., missing covariates rules) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2015 Grade 9 South Africa national report uses five plausible values to summarize mathematics and science achievement and applies multilevel (HLM) modeling to explain mathematics achievement. For learner contextual factors, the multilevel results show that higher SES and more frequent speaking of the test language are associated with higher mathematics scores, while older age, female gender, and bullying victimization are associated with lower scores (e.g., age −16.19 per additional year; test-language fluency +14.80). For school factors, the final model indicates that fee-paying and independent schools have higher average mathematics achievement than no-fee schools, but a substantial portion of the gap is explained by school resources and especially school climate; bullying frequency is strongly negative (−14.11, p<0.001). The report emphasizes that all analyses are cross-sectional, limiting causal interpretation of the associations between school resources/climate and achievement.
